text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
* Banco Finantia is considering applying to be listed on Lisbon bourse, its president Antonio Guerreiro told the paper.

* Former president Mario Soares criticised proposals to revise the constitution. He told Antena 1 radio in an interview that he was against plans to give emigrants the right to vote for the presidency.
* The government plans to raise the public sector minimum wage to 59,300 escudos per month from the present level of 56,700.
* Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said the restructuring of the pulp and paper sector will include privatisations of pulp companies in 1998.
* The banking sector grew by 50 percent in the first six months of the year, boosted by commissions from the privatisation of utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal.

* TAP-Air Portugal transported 1.89 million passengers in the first six months of 1997, a 9.7 percent increase over the same period of 1996. Talks between pilots and TAP management to seek an end to a conflict over pilots' working hours are due to resume in Lisbon on Monday afternoon.
* Portuguese companies which are being privatised are good investments, according to a study by U.S. financial markets research company Kuett Group.
